children: SpaceX moves fast. It's working to secure access to cell towers just weeks after buying more wireless spectrum. Both steps move Elon Musk's rocket and AI company closer to becoming a full-service wireless telecom provider.
The moves are upending wireless stocks.
Thursday, Bloomberg reported that SpaceX is looking for access to 80,000 cell sites in the U.S., mentioning cell tower real estate investment trust Crown Castle by name.
SpaceX and Crown Castle didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

The report sent shares of Crown Castle up 7.7% in premarket trading on Friday, while S&P 500 futures were down 0.2%. SpaceX stock was up 1.5% at $146.97. Shares of American Tower and SBA Communications, two other cell tower REITs, were up 5.5% and 5.4%, respectively.

Coming into Friday trading, shares of the three REITs were up 9% on average since Oct. 9, the day after SpaceX announced its purchase of low-band spectrum from Grain Management. The spectrum band penetrates obstacles such as buildings and brought SpaceX one step closer to offering mobile service, directly competing with the traditional industry.
Shares of wireless telecoms Verizon Communications, AT&T, and T-Mobile US were down an average of 6% since the announcement. All three stocks were off again early Friday, between 3% and 5%.

SpaceX already has an impressive communications business. It has more than 11,000 satellites in low-Earth orbit, providing Starlink broadband service to more than 13.5 million customers in 174 countries. SpaceX's connectivity business generated third-quarter sales and Ebitda of $5.2 billion and $3.5 billion, respectively.
AT&T, for comparison, generated third-quarter Ebitda of about $12.5 billion, up 5% year over year. SpaceX's connectivity Ebitda grew 82% year over year.
SpaceX's size, speed, and ambitions are frightening traditional wireless investors. Its mobile wireless goals have been no secret, but they are advancing faster than anyone expected.

Eventually, SpaceX might need more wireless spectrum — essentially the pipes that carry wireless signals and data — to compete with the big three. SpaceX has amassed about 80 megahertz of spectrum, according to T-Mobile, which has closer to 400 megahertz.
